title: Traits from laws of growth are later co-opted by descendants

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Traits from laws of growth are later co-opted by descendants

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Many modifications arose wholly from laws of growth and were at first of no advantage to a species, but were later taken advantage of by its further modified descendants, as skull sutures that arose in egg-laying animals were later used in mammalian birth.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we may confidently believe that many modifications, wholly due to the laws of growth, and at first in no way advantageous to a species, have been subsequently taken advantage of by the still further modified descendants of this species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Organs of small importance.”. Scope: plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Exaptation can be tested for well-documented traits using morphology, fossils, and phylogeny. Existing data cannot establish the proposed initial cause or frequency across 'many modifications.'

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the origin, ancestral function, and later use of candidate traits on phylogenies, testing whether traits predate the ecology in which they became advantageous. Temporal precedence and later functional recruitment support co-option.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Laws of growth' requires modern reinterpretation.

Initial absence of advantage is difficult to infer.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.45
data existence: 0.64
analysis feasibility: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The skull-suture example can be examined as a timing-of-function question with existing trees and matrices, but only after substantial interpretation of what 'laws of growth' and 'at first of no advantage' mean. The quantitative claim that many modifications follow this path has no dataset. Even a clear sequence would not separate later co-option from an earlier, undetected function.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On an amniote tree, date the origin of skull sutures relative to live birth and ask whether sutures are present in egg-laying relatives that do not use them in parturition. Origin of the trait before its mammalian use supports co-option in that example; a suture system that appears with live birth would count against it. 'Many modifications' would further require a frequency across traits.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Original lack of advantage is a historical negative that current non-use does not prove.

No catalog records which modifications began as non-adaptive byproducts.

Suture function during birth is not a field in trait databases.
